newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria offers concessions on its gas pipelines.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria offers concessions on its gas pipelines.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet decided on Sunday to offer pipeline concessions for transiting Russian gas through its territory and will call two tenders within a month, government officials said.

"The cabinet decided to offer a concession on the existing transit gas pipelines and another concession on pipelines planned to be built," head of Bulgaria's concession department Nikola Baltov told a news conference after the cabinet session.
Baltov said a concession of 35 years will be granted to the winners of the tenders, who will be announced within three months after launching the tenders.
Bulgaria has a 2,200-km pipeline network, including 625 km of transit pipelines which receive and transmit gas from outside the country.

Bulgaria transits Russian gas to Turkey and Greece and its pipeline to Macedonia has been constructed and filled with gas but is still waiting for its western neighbours to complete the pipeline on their territory.
"The concession for existing transit pipelines includes the pipelines to Turkey, Greece and Macedonia," Petar Sabev, executive director of Bulgaria's gas monopolist Bulgargas, told Reuters.
He said the cabinet had also decided to reduce the assets of Bulgargas, which owns the existing pipelines, by the cost of the pipelines.

Participants in the two tenders should present a banking guarantee of $5 million and prove their ability to transit the necessary volumes through direct contracts with Russia's gas giant Gazprom, gas officials said.

The winner of the tender for enlarging the gas transit system on Bulgarian territory, which is expected to cost some $500 million, will operate it under the formula build-operate-transfer, Baltov said.
In July, the Bulgarian government decided to open a procedure for granting a concession to the Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy, which was set up last year by Gazprom and Bulgargas.
"Topenergy is a serious candidate and it has great chances (in winning the tenders)," energy minister Roumen Ovcharov told reporters.
Gazprom has 50 percent in Topenergy and Bulgargas holds a 25.1 percent stake. The remaining 24.9 percent are distributed among Bulgarian banks and firms.
